_meta.indication: VENCLEXTA is a BCL-2 inhibitor indicated for the treatment of patients with chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) with 17p deletion, as detected by an FDA approved test, who have received at least one prior therapy.

pivotal_trials.design: Open-label, single-arm, multicenter trial; no control group (historical response rates used for comparison).
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with relapsed or refractory CLL with 17p deletion who had received at least one prior therapy.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Overall response rate (ORR = CR+CRi+nPR+PR) as assessed by the IRC.
pivotal_trials.n: 106 patients with 17p deletion (main cohort 107 enrolled; 106 with confirmed 17p deletion used for labeling).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥20%) were neutropenia, diarrhea, nausea, anemia, upper respiratory tract infection, thrombocytopenia, and fatigue. Grade 3 or 4 neutropenia occurred in 41% (98/240). Serious adverse reactions were reported in 43.8% of patients. Key risks are tumor lysis syndrome and neutropenia.
target_moa: Venetoclax is a first-in-class, oral small molecule inhibitor of the BCL-2 (B-cell lymphoma protein 2) anti-apoptotic protein; CLL cells are almost universally dependent on BCL-2, so its inhibition can restore apoptosis in CLL cells.
companion_dx_detail: 17p deletion confirmed in peripheral blood specimens using the Vysis CLL FISH Probe Kit, which is FDA approved for selection of patients for VENCLEXTA treatment.

advisory_committee.vote: An Advisory Committee Meeting was not planned for this application because the Division of Hematology Products was familiar with the trial design and clinical trial endpoints.
